page: Microsoft Azure E32s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv7 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance features 32 virtual CPUs derived from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This virtual machine does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in specific workloads. The server achieves a strong rating in static web serving throughput at 43.89 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression at 35.62 GB/sec. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 181.75 GB/sec for read operations and 77.85 GB/sec for write operations. In terms of computational benchmarks, the instance registers a passmark CPU score of 47694.11 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 31862.21. Large language model inference benchmarks show strong prompt processing speeds of 186.24 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model and 298.63 tokens/sec for text generation using a small 135M model.

From a resource density perspective, the E32s_v7 offers high memory capacity relative to its compute resources, making it a cost-efficient option for memory-bound workloads that do not require local ephemeral storage. The lack of local storage requires relying entirely on external Premium Storage, which represents a key architectural tradeoff. The hardware features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations. This server is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, static web serving, and moderate-scale language model inference.
